data.narrative: The student correctly identified and articulated the swallowed exception anti-pattern, explaining how a silent try/catch creates a disconnect between response code and actual DB state. They demonstrated solid production reasoning by connecting exception propagation to the global filter pattern and explaining exactly what gets logged vs suppressed. The reflect answers showed understanding of why logging rules (log context, never input data) matter for incident response without creating security risks.

dimension_scores.observation: Correctly explained the tradeoff between swallowing exceptions (hides failures from callers) vs propagating them (loud but diagnosable). Connected graceful degradation to the specific cost — silent 200s masking writes that never happened.
dimension_scores.evidence: POST /links returns 200 but GET /links shows record never saved — the student identified this as the symptom of a swallowed exception before seeing the code.

dimension_scores.observation: Used hints strategically (compare response vs DB state, search for try/catch around write), formed a hypothesis, and confirmed it by inspecting the service code. Fix was targeted — remove the swallowing catch, let propagation reach the global filter.
dimension_scores.evidence: Diagnosed: 'try/catch wraps DB write in create(), catches error silently, returns 200 with empty/partial response — record never persisted.'

dimension_scores.observation: Explicitly stated that the fix must include redaction — only structured fields (request_id, route, status_code) logged for 500s, never the error message, stack trace, or input data. Proved with sentinel test: DO_NOT_LOG_ME_123 absent from all log output.
dimension_scores.evidence: Sentinel test: Authorization: Bearer DO_NOT_LOG_ME_123 — logs show only request_id/route/status_code/latency_ms, sentinel absent.

dimension_scores.observation: Built and verified the full error envelope contract (error.code, error.message, error.request_id) with concrete curl output for all three test cases. Identified remaining risk: without explicit timeouts, production failures can become mystery hangs.
dimension_scores.evidence: 400 BAD_REQUEST response: {error:{code:BAD_REQUEST,message:Invalid request,request_id:5148158f-...}} — no stack trace, request_id present, matches log entry.

dimension_scores.observation: Explained error flow in a clear sequence: (1) exception thrown → (2) propagates to filter → (3) filter maps to safe envelope → (4) logs structured context. Used concrete field names throughout.
dimension_scores.evidence: Error flow: linkModel.create() throws → propagates to HttpExceptionFilter(@Catch()) → maps to 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR envelope with request_id → logs request_id+route+status_code.

strengths: Sentinel testing: proactively proved secrets not logged by using a sentinel value (DO_NOT_LOG_ME_123) — a production verification technique, not just code review
Error envelope consistency: every error response (400, 500) uses the same {error:{code,message,request_id}} shape, proven with three different curl tests
data.recommendation: In Module 06, apply the same structured thinking to timeouts: define what timeout value is appropriate per operation type (DB query vs external HTTP call vs queue drain) before writing any timeout code.

public_evidence.artifact: Global exception filter + request ID middleware
public_evidence.student_action: Built @Catch() global exception filter that maps all errors to safe envelopes with stable error.code, error.message, error.request_id. Added request ID middleware that logs request_id, route, status_code, latency_ms per request.
public_evidence.technical_detail: src/common/filters/http-exception.filter.ts — @Catch(), safeParse, process.exit on unknown; src/common/middleware/request-id.middleware.ts — randomUUID(), res.locals.requestId, finish event logging
public_evidence.proof: POST /links with not-a-url → HTTP 400, body: {error:{code:BAD_REQUEST,message:Invalid request,request_id:5148158f-623d-43c4-9028-39d1f7621ccd}}, log: request_id:5148158f-..., route:/links, status_code:400, latency_ms:6
public_evidence.ability: Implements consistent error handling and structured request logging for production APIs
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows understanding that every 4xx/5xx must include a correlation ID so users can report issues and engineers can find the matching log line within seconds

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Correctly identified from hints alone: try/catch around DB write hides failure, returns 200 when write failed
@Catch() with safeParse + process.exit flow — catches all unhandled exceptions before they leak details
Sentinel test proved Authorization header value never appears in logs

teaching_approaches.detail: Compare response vs DB state — POST returns 200 but record not in DB

learning_style_signals: responds well to concrete curl output as proof
